items.title: Section: Compassion Gathers In Every Wholesome Practice, and Its Fourfold Benefit Closes the Entire Chapter — "Bodhisattva Awakening Is Built by Compassion"

items.zh: 菩薩如是以所修悲熏修心故，於內外事，無有少分而不能捨；無戒律儀而不能學；無他怨害而不能忍；無有精進而不能起；無有靜慮而不能證，無有妙慧而不能入。是故如來，若有請問菩薩菩提誰所建立？皆正答言：菩薩菩提悲所建立。如前所說一一無量，皆有無量菩薩如意圓德隨轉，皆能攝受無量愛果，皆無量種一向妙善無罪隨轉。當知菩薩精勤修習如是無量，能得四種功德勝利。謂由修習此無量故，先得最勝現法樂住；攝受、增長無量最勝福德資糧；能於無上正等菩提意樂堅固；為欲饒益諸有情故，於生死中，堪能忍受一切大苦。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, in this way, infuse their own mind through cultivated compassion find that there is not the smallest portion of any internal or external matter they cannot give up; no precept or vow they cannot train in; no hostility or harm from another they cannot bear; no diligence they cannot summon; no meditative concentration they cannot attain; no subtle wisdom they cannot penetrate. For this reason, whenever the Tathāgata is asked who actually builds a bodhisattva's awakening, the correct answer given is always this: a bodhisattva's awakening is built by compassion. Because bodhisattvas cultivate these immeasurables, they first obtain the most excellent present ease; they gather in and increase boundless, most excellent provisions of merit; they fix their aspiration towards supreme, complete awakening firmly in place; and, wishing to benefit all sentient beings, they become genuinely capable of enduring every great suffering throughout birth and death.

items.title: Section: Chapter Seventeen Opens — the Factors of Awakening, Fifteen Topics Named in a Single Verse, Spanning This Fascicle and the Two That Follow

items.zh: 云何菩薩菩提分法？嗢拕南曰：慚愧、堅力持、無厭、論世智、正依、無礙解、資糧、菩提分、止觀、性巧便、陀羅尼、正願、三摩地有三、法嗢拕南四。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter seventeen, part one: the factors of awakening. What are a bodhisattva's own factors of awakening? A summary verse states: "Conscience and shame; firm resolve; a tireless mind; skill in treatises; skill in worldly knowledge — correct reliance; unhindered understanding; provisions; the factors of awakening; calming and insight; the nature of skilful means; mnemonic retention; correct aspiration; the three concentrations; and dharma-summaries, four in number."

items.title: Section: Conscience and Shame Opens the Factors of Awakening — Blushing Before Oneself, and Blushing Before the Noble

items.zh: 云何名為菩薩慚愧？當知慚愧略有二種。一者、自性，二者、依處。言自性者，謂諸菩薩於罪現行，能正覺知我為非法，內生羞恥，是名為慚。即於其中能正覺知，於他敬畏，外生羞恥，是名為愧。菩薩羞恥，本性猛利，況復修習。如是應知名為菩薩慚愧自性。
items.en: What is called a bodhisattva's conscience and shame? One should understand that conscience and shame are, in brief, of two kinds: first, intrinsic nature; second, its basis. As for intrinsic nature: bodhisattvas who, when wrongdoing actually occurs, correctly recognise "I have acted wrongly," and give rise to shame from within themselves — this is called conscience. Correctly recognising that very same wrongdoing, but through reverent fear of others, giving rise to shame from without — this is called shame proper. A bodhisattva's own capacity for shame is, by its very nature, already forceful — how much more so, then, once it has been further cultivated through practice. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's intrinsic nature of conscience and shame.

items.title: Section: Four Occasions for Genuine Shame — Failing to Act, Acting Wrongly, Hiding a Fault, and Carrying an Unresolved Regret

items.zh: 言依處者，略有四種。若諸菩薩，於所應作不隨建立而生羞恥，當知是名第一依處。若諸菩薩，於不應作隨順建立而生羞恥，當知是名第二依處。若諸菩薩，於覆己惡而生羞恥，當知是名第三依處。若諸菩薩，於自所生惡作有依隨逐不捨而生羞恥，當知是名第四依處。如是應知名為菩薩慚愧依處。
items.en: As for its basis, this is, in brief, of four kinds. Bodhisattvas who give rise to shame over failing to establish action they genuinely should have undertaken — one should understand this to be called the first basis. Bodhisattvas who give rise to shame over establishing, in accordance with wrong causes and conditions, action they genuinely should not have undertaken — one should understand this to be called the second basis. Bodhisattvas who give rise to shame over concealing their own faults — one should understand this to be called the third basis. Bodhisattvas who give rise to shame over a self-produced regret that continues to follow them without being released — one should understand this to be called the fourth basis. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's basis of conscience and shame.

items.title: Section: Firm Resolve Opens — Restraining Defiled Tendencies, Enduring Eight Kinds of Suffering, and Standing Unmoved Before Five Classical Fears

items.zh: 云何菩薩堅力持性？當知此性略有二種。一者、自性，二者、依處。言自性者，謂能禁制染污心性，不隨煩惱自在行性，堪忍苦性，種種眾多猛利怖畏雖現在前而正加行無傾動性。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's firm resolve? One should understand that this quality is, in brief, of two kinds: first, intrinsic nature; second, its basis. As for intrinsic nature: the capacity to restrain a defiled tendency of mind, the capacity not to let affliction act freely, the capacity to bear suffering, and the capacity to remain genuinely unshaken in one's own correct practice even when a great variety of intensely severe fears actually confront one directly. This is called the intrinsic nature of firm resolve.

items.title: Section: Firm Resolve's Cause — Courageous Vigour Joined With Correct Discernment; Then Five Trials That Actually Call It Forth

items.zh: 性勇相應，能正思擇，是故得成堅力持性。如是名為堅力持性自性。如是菩薩堅力持性，略說應知有五依處。一者、會遇生死輪轉種種大苦所化有情種種邪行；二者、為益諸有情故，誓受長時生死流轉；三者、遭遇異論朋黨諍競難詰，及處大眾宣揚法義；四者、誓受一切菩薩所應學處；五者、聽聞廣大甚深難思議法。是名堅力持性依處。
items.en: Being joined with courageous vigour and correctly discerning, one thereby accomplishes firm resolve. This firm resolve of bodhisattvas, in brief, should be understood to have five bases: first, encountering the various wrong conduct of beings undergoing the great suffering of the wandering through birth and death that one is guiding them out of; second, vowing to endure prolonged wandering through birth and death for the sake of benefiting beings; third, encountering hostile factions and difficult challenges in debate, and expounding the meaning of the dharma before a great assembly; fourth, vowing to undertake every discipline a bodhisattva should train in; fifth, hearing the vast, profound, and scarcely conceivable teaching. This is called the basis of firm resolve.

items.title: Section: A Tireless Mind — Five Causes, From Inborn Strength to a Compassion So Forceful It Never Notices the Effort

items.zh: 云何菩薩心無厭倦？當知菩薩由五因緣，普於一切正加行中，心無厭倦。一者、菩薩性自有力，故無厭倦。二者、菩薩即於如是無厭倦心數數串習，故無厭倦。三者、菩薩方便攝受精進勇猛，能正隨觀前後所得展轉殊勝，故無厭倦。四者、菩薩成就猛利增上妙慧正思擇力，故無厭倦。五者、菩薩於諸有情猛利悲心、極哀愍心恒常現前，故無厭倦。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's tireless mind? One should understand that bodhisattvas, through five causes and conditions, remain tireless throughout every correct practice they undertake. First, bodhisattvas are, by their own inborn nature, already forceful, and are therefore tireless. Second, bodhisattvas, by repeatedly habituating themselves to this very tireless mind, are therefore tireless. Third, bodhisattvas, skilfully sustaining courageous diligence, correctly observe how what they have attained grows progressively more excellent from one stage to the next, and are therefore tireless. Fourth, bodhisattvas, accomplishing a forceful, heightened, and subtle wisdom's power of correct discernment, are therefore tireless. Fifth, bodhisattvas, with a forceful compassion and the deepest sympathetic care constantly present towards all sentient beings, are therefore tireless.

items.title: Section: Skill in Treatises Opens — Fluent Mastery of the Five Branches of Classical Learning Through Genuine Study and Reflection

items.zh: 云何菩薩善知諸論？謂諸菩薩，於五明處名句文身相應諸法，從他善受，言善通利。即於如是諸法妙義，或從他所善聽善決，或自專精善擇善思，如是知法知義菩薩，於法於義為不忘失，恒常精勤，不捨加行。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's skill in treatises? Bodhisattvas who properly receive, from another, every teaching belonging to the five branches of classical learning, expressed through name, phrase, and syllable, and become genuinely fluent in its words. Regarding the wondrous meaning of these very teachings, whether by properly hearing it explained and properly resolved by another, or by properly discerning and properly reflecting on it through one's own focused effort, bodhisattvas who thus know the teaching and know its meaning, so as never to forget either the teaching or its meaning, remain constantly diligent, never abandoning this ongoing effort.

blocks.text: The chapter on the immeasurables closes with a famous line; then the chapter on the **factors of awakening** opens, with qualities that will run through fascicle 46.

With a mind infused by compassion, "there is not the smallest thing, inner or outer, they cannot give up; no precept they cannot keep". "Whenever the Tathāgata is asked who builds a bodhisattva's awakening, the answer is: a bodhisattva's awakening is built by compassion."

A verse names fifteen topics, spanning this fascicle and the next two: conscience and shame, firm resolve, tirelessness, skill in treatises, knowledge of the world, the four reliances, and more. Venerable Miào Jìng: awakening is the fruit; the factors are its causes.

"Recognising 'I have acted wrongly' and feeling shame within is conscience; feeling shame through reverent fear of others is shame." Four occasions: failing to act when one should; acting wrongly; hiding a fault; unresolved regret. Venerable Miào Jìng: someone who keeps committing faults cannot be said to have conscience.
"Restraining defiled tendencies, not letting affliction act freely, bearing suffering, unshaken before fear." Venerable Miào Jìng: with wisdom one observes the matter, and observing dissolves it.
Five causes, from innate strength to "forceful compassion and deep care constantly present". Venerable Miào Jìng: one is physical strength, one mental.
Mastery of the five fields "expressed through name, phrase, and syllable".

quiz.q: When the Tathāgata is asked who builds a bodhisattva's awakening, how does he answer?
options: a bodhisattva's awakening is built by compassion
quiz.why: "Whenever the Tathāgata is asked who builds a bodhisattva's awakening, the correct answer given is always this: a bodhisattva's awakening is built by compassion." Venerable Miào Jìng: delusion cannot free beings; subtle wisdom is needed — compassion-infused practice brings all the perfections.

quiz.q: At the opening of the chapter on factors of awakening, how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "factors of awakening"?
options: awakening is the fruit, "factors" the causes — causes of supreme awakening
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: awakening is the fruit, the "factors" are causes — causes of supreme awakening. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas must cultivate fifteen qualities, all causes of awakening.

quiz.q: How does the treatise distinguish conscience from shame?
options: shame from within on recognising wrong is conscience; shame from without through reverent fear of others is shame
quiz.why: Recognising "I have acted wrongly" and feeling shame within is conscience; feeling shame without, through reverent fear of others, is shame. Venerable Miào Jìng and Master Cháng Bǎi agree: conscience faces oneself, shame faces others.

quiz.q: The fourth basis — "regret with a support, following and not released." The English drops "with a support." How do the lectures explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: the four requisites; Cháng Bǎi: first "regretting, then doing it again — the later deed relies on the earlier," then cites the four-requisites reading
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the four supports are robes, food, bedding, and medicine. Master Cháng Bǎi gives a second reading — regretting a wrong, then repeating it, the later deed relying on the earlier — and also cites the four-requisites reading. The English omits "with a support."

quiz.q: What four capacities make up the intrinsic nature of firm resolve?
options: restraining defilement, not letting affliction act freely, bearing suffering, unshaken before fear
quiz.why: Restraining defiled tendencies, not letting affliction act freely, bearing suffering, and remaining unshaken in correct practice before intense fears. Master Cháng Bǎi: greed when one feels like it, anger when one feels like it, with no reason at all — that is "affliction acting freely."

quiz.q: "Joined with courageous vigour and correctly discerning." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "correctly discerning"?
options: this is wisdom — observing the matter with great wisdom dissolves it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "correctly discerning" is wisdom — with great wisdom one observes the matter, and observing it dissolves it. Master Cháng Bǎi: "joined with courageous vigour" means having the disposition of the perfection of diligence.

quiz.q: What is the fifth of the five causes of a tireless mind?
options: forceful compassion and deepest care constantly present towards beings
quiz.why: "Fifth, with forceful compassion and the deepest care constantly present towards all beings, they are tireless." Venerable Miào Jìng: when compassion arises, weariness is forgotten.
